title: implement Linear

atoms.evidence: out = x @ self.weight.T; if self.bias is not None: out = out + self.bias — exact 'x @ W.T + b' affine forward, using the custom Tensor's @ and .T
sf = in_features**-0.5; self.weight = Parameter(Tensor(sf * (2 * np.random.rand(out_features, in_features) - 1))) — uniform in [-sf, sf] with sf = 1/sqrt(in_features)

self.weight = Parameter(Tensor(sf * (2 * np.random.rand(...) - 1))); self.bias = Parameter(Tensor(...)) — the Parameter(Tensor(np.random...)) two-step wrap explicitly required by markdown: 'Don't forget to wrap your weights as Parameter(Tensor(...))'
class Linear(Module): weight: Parameter; bias: Parameter | None — Parameter type annotations and instantiation; test asserts isinstance(linear.weight, Tensor) and linear.weight.requires_grad
class Linear(Module): super().__init__() — inherits from the hand-rolled Module class; ReLU(Module) and MLP(Module) shown below
Same nn.Module subclass pattern applied to the custom Module: override __init__/forward, call super().__init__() (R9.3 cross-part reuse)
Parameter wraps learnable tensors so Module.parameters() finds them (R9.2 cross-part reuse — semantics identical to torch.nn.Parameter)
Tensor(sf * (2 * np.random.rand(...) - 1)) — ndarray-backed Tensor construction throughout init
